transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stay focused on the actual experiment anymore. In a grant call or a safety meeting, I’ll notice a pump vibration, something a student says, or an odd peak in an old spectrum, and then I’m off following that for hours. Meanwhile, the thing everyone needed me to do just falls apart.
Have these difficulties with focus and distraction been present since childhood, or did they begin more recently?
It’s more recent. It started about seven months ago, around when I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
How has your mood generally been over these past several months?

For months I’ve felt almost electrified, like the lab is finally moving at my speed. But if someone questions my plan or tells me to slow down, I snap at them. It’s gotten bad enough that some of the students seem to avoid coming to my office.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt deeply depressed or lost interest in your usual activities?
I’m not sure. I don’t remember having a stretch like that before this.
Before these past seven months, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt unusually energized, high, or wired like this?
I don’t think so. I can’t recall another time when I felt this revved up for this long.
